criterion: Canonical sources have unique identifiers and retain provenance, publisher, period, geography, scope, access status, and evidence role.
rationale: The canonical registry provides sufficient source-level provenance for controlled extraction.
analytical_implication: Numerical observations can be linked back to a defined source without relying on undocumented source identity.

criterion: Potential analytical uses are evaluated separately from source availability and source identity.
rationale: The assessment distinguishes usable, caveated, contextual, and ineligible analytical uses.
analytical_implication: A source being available does not make every metric or inference from that source eligible.

criterion: Material measurement, comparability, regulatory, cost, and evidence decisions retain rationale and analytical implications.
rationale: Material decisions are documented independently from individual source records.
analytical_implication: Later extraction and analysis can apply consistent rules and retain decision traceability.

criterion: Verified evidence exists for driver earnings or source-reported income across multiple research sources.
rationale: Multiple sources contain earnings evidence, but definitions, periods, geography, sampling design, and denominators differ.
analytical_implication: Earnings must be extracted using source-defined concepts before any cross-source comparison is attempted.

criterion: Evidence exists for relevant workload measures such as orders, distance, workdays, or working-time measures.
rationale: Useful workload evidence exists, but time and distance definitions are not fully standardized across sources.
analytical_implication: Online, productive, and source-reported working hours must remain distinct; paid-trip distance cannot silently represent total work-related distance.

criterion: Evidence exists for operating-cost concepts relevant to fuel, maintenance, vehicle costs, communication costs, and other work-related costs.
rationale: Cost concepts are covered, but some research sources bundle work-related costs with personal consumption or broader expenditure.
analytical_implication: Only cost components consistent with the project operating-cost boundary may enter net operating earnings.

criterion: Regulatory, official implementation, platform-stated, driver-reported, and realized deduction evidence are treated as separate evidence layers.
rationale: Several deduction-related sources exist, but strong matched transaction-level realized deductions remain limited.
analytical_implication: Regulatory ceilings, platform policies, and self-reported deduction brackets cannot substitute for observed realized deductions.

criterion: Historical and current regulatory evidence is documented with period, service-scope, and legal-status boundaries.
rationale: The historical framework is verifiable, while the primary text of KP-PHB 532/2026 was not publicly verified as of the Stage 1 retrieval date.
analytical_implication: KP-PHB 532/2026 is not an authoritative legal input; 2026 implementation statements remain a separate contextual evidence layer.

criterion: A redistributable official regulatory document used as historical evidence is preserved in the repository.
rationale: KP 564/2022 is preserved as an official period-bound regulatory source.
analytical_implication: The historical regulated cost structure and fee ceiling can be independently inspected.

criterion: Fuel-cost modelling requires fuel product, effective date, and geography to match the driver observation.
rationale: The matching rule is established, but additional period-specific fuel-price observations may be required after numerical extraction reveals the exact observation periods and locations.
analytical_implication: No single national fuel price may be applied across incompatible products, dates, or geographies.

criterion: Official CPI evidence is available for transparent real-value transformations when geography and period are compatible.
rationale: Official province and city CPI sources are available, but transformation eligibility depends on the geography and period of each extracted monetary observation.
analytical_implication: Nominal source values remain authoritative; inflation adjustment is a documented derived transformation.

criterion: Sampling design and representativeness limitations are preserved for survey and interview evidence.
rationale: The evidence base distinguishes probability, purposive, local, and small interview samples and records their inferential limits.
analytical_implication: Convenience, purposive, local, or small interview samples are not nationally representative by default.

criterion: Source provenance is retained without requiring redistribution of documents whose reuse rights are not established.
rationale: The evidence architecture permits link/provenance treatment and structured extraction while reserving raw-file storage for defensibly redistributable material.
analytical_implication: Restricted or externally hosted source documents do not need to be copied into the repository for their eligible observations to remain traceable.

criterion: Litbang Kompas 2026 secondary summaries are excluded from quantitative primary-evidence roles because the original survey methodology and final source definitions were not independently verified.
rationale: Secondary reports contain unresolved differences in sample count and survey-method descriptions, while the original methodology is not available under the project evidence standard.
analytical_implication: Litbang Kompas 2026 may provide context only and must not supply primary quantitative observations for the project dataset.

criterion: KP-PHB 532/2026 is excluded from authoritative legal-rule use until the primary legal text and full operative scope are publicly verifiable.
rationale: Multiple statements reference the instrument or an 8% implementation, but the primary legal text was not publicly verified during Stage 1.
analytical_implication: An 8% figure cannot be treated as a universal legal benchmark or realized driver deduction.

criterion: The evidence base is sufficient to begin structured extraction despite the absence of a robust same-observation chain covering gross service earnings, realized deduction, driver receipt, and all operating costs.
rationale: The project has substantial component-level evidence, but no single verified source currently measures the full unit-economics chain with consistent definitions.
analytical_implication: Later net-earnings construction must distinguish observed components from derived or scenario inputs and must not fabricate a matched transaction chain.

criterion: Source coverage, provenance, analytical eligibility, comparability constraints, and material methodological decisions are sufficiently defined for structured numerical extraction.
rationale: No unresolved issue blocks structured extraction, but important evidence limitations remain and must stay binding in subsequent stages.
analytical_implication: Stage 1 is complete with caveats; later work must preserve source-specific definitions and the documented evidence boundaries.
